title: Morbius
synopsis: Michael and Milo grow up depending on transfusions. Michael becomes a doctor, but his experimental treatment leaves him craving blood and puts others in danger.
verdictRationale: As a child, Michael repairs Milo’s medical equipment with a pen spring. As a doctor, he must face a harder question: who bears the cost of his own recovery? His wish to heal is understandable. The deaths following his experiment make the price of pursuing it impossible to dismiss.
ageRationale: The film dwells on a child losing access to a transfusion, transformed faces, neck wounds and people being stalked for blood. These images may be especially difficult for teens familiar with hospital treatment.
reflection: Michael’s earliest act of healing is also his least spectacular. He sees the boy beside him in danger and uses what he has. Families can ask what it takes to keep that same attention on the patient when the promise of a discovery becomes more exciting.

questions: What does the broken machine tell us about Michael and Milo before either has powers?
What does the doctor see in Michael that a medical chart could miss?

title: Madame Web
synopsis: A paramedic begins seeing possible futures. When a stranger hunts three teenage girls because of what he believes they will do, Cassie takes them into her care.
verdictRationale: Cassie gives the girls something her visions alone cannot give them: a skill they can use for someone else. The rescue at the end pays off that quiet lesson. Her growing willingness to depend on the three girls makes her care for them credible.
ageRationale: A man repeatedly attacks teenagers in visions, including a neck-breaking assault. Knowing that Cassie can sometimes change the outcome may offer little comfort while a child is watching. Drowning and attempted resuscitation recur.
reflection: Cassie has every reason to think of herself as the rescuer. By teaching the girls, she makes room for a different kind of family, one in which she can receive care as well as give it.
